## Data Cleaning and Preprocessing Overview

This section explains how the Lightcast 2024 job postings dataset was cleaned and prepared for analysis. The goal of the data preparation process was to remove unnecessary or redundant fields, handle missing values, standardize important variables, and create a cleaner dataset that could be used for exploratory analysis, skill gap analysis, and predictive modeling.

Because the original dataset contains many detailed classification fields, several redundant NAICS and SOC code columns were reviewed and simplified. These fields represent different levels of the same industry and occupational classification systems. Keeping every version would make the dataset more complex without adding much value to the analysis. Therefore, the cleaned dataset keeps the most useful classification fields while removing unnecessary duplicates.

The cleaning process also included reviewing missing values, removing duplicate job postings, correcting placeholder values, and preparing variables needed for later analysis. These steps helped make the dataset more reliable for comparing AI-related and non-AI careers across industries, occupations, skills, education requirements, and experience levels.

# Logistic Regression was used to predict whether a job posting was AI-related or non-AI-related. The model attempted to identify whether education requirements, experience requirements, and occupational classifications could distinguish AI-focused jobs from traditional jobs. The model used MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE, MIN_EDULEVELS, SOC_ENC, and ONET_ENC. These variables were selected because they represent the educational, experiential, and occupational characteristics commonly associated with workforce qualifications. The Logistic Regression model struggled to accurately identify AI-related jobs due to the relatively small proportion of AI postings within the dataset. This finding suggests that AI-related jobs cannot be identified solely by broad occupational classifications and minimum qualification requirements. For job seekers, this implies that AI careers are often differentiated by specialized skills and knowledge that are not fully captured by traditional occupation codes alone.

# Figure 4. AI Job Postings by Education Requirement. The proportion of AI-related postings generally increases with educational requirements, suggesting that AI careers are concentrated among jobs requiring advanced qualifications.

# Key Insights AI-related jobs represented approximately 4% of all job postings in the dataset, indicating that while AI careers continue to expand, they remain a specialized segment of the labor market. KMeans clustering identified five distinct occupational groups, suggesting that labor-market opportunities naturally separate into different occupational segments. The classification models demonstrated that education and experience requirements were the strongest predictors of AI-related positions. Random Forest feature importance results showed that minimum years of experience and minimum education level accounted for nearly all predictive power, while occupational classification variables contributed relatively little. The results suggest that AI-related careers are differentiated primarily by higher qualification requirements rather than broad occupational categories. Individuals pursuing AI-related careers may therefore benefit more from acquiring specialized skills, advanced education, and relevant experience than from changing occupational categories alone. Individuals interested in AI-related careers should focus on developing specialized technical skills and gaining relevant experience, as these factors were the strongest predictors of AI-related job postings. Employers appear to place significant value on prior experience and educational attainment when hiring for AI-focused roles. Job seekers currently working in analytical, technical, or data-oriented occupations may find it easier to transition into AI-related positions because many AI jobs require transferable quantitative and problem-solving skills. Pursuing certifications, advanced coursework, and hands-on projects involving machine learning, data analytics, or artificial intelligence can improve competitiveness in this growing labor-market segment. Given the relatively small proportion of AI-related postings observed in the dataset, job seekers should also maintain flexibility by developing skills that are applicable across both AI and traditional occupations.
